name: SpaceX
bio: SpaceX designs, manufactures and launches the world’s most advanced rockets and spacecraft

recentPosts.text:
On Starship’s 15th flight last week, the Super Heavy booster correctly performed a safe abort when returning for a catch and ended its mission with a splashdown in the water off the coast of Starbase. Following splashdown, SpaceX recovery teams were immediately onsite to safe the area while our Environmental Health and Safety team worked to ensure any debris that washes onshore was recovered → https://t.co/ALNcWBQinC

When we received reports of potential debris in Mexican territory, we immediately mobilized to send specialists to aid in identification and lead any cleanup work required, just as we did on Boca Chica Beach near Starbase. We continue to stay in contact with the Mexican government and are on standby to send support if authorities in Mexico tell us it is actually needed. Partners on the ground relayed that theyhave found very little debris in their sweeps of the beach, and the small amount they have found are not clearly from SpaceX operations.

The majority of the social media posts online claiming widespread debris and damage are either outright fabrications or intentionally misleading. As repeatedly stated, independent tests conducted on materials inside Starship and the Super Heavy booster, including toxicity analyses, confirm they pose no chemical, biological, or toxicological risks.

Starship is designed to be fully reusable, with future missions planning to return all hardware back to the launch site for catch and reuse. SpaceX is the only one, whether company or country, that has demonstrated this capability is now possible.

As Texas communities consider major supercomputing investments, careful long-term tax planning is essential. Under Texas’s no-new-revenue tax framework, rising property values generally drive tax rates down. But as expensive computing equipment rapidly depreciates, this can create significant year-to-year swings in property tax rates and a potential future revenue cliff.

The proposed abatement was designed to address this challenge: provide the County with substantial, predictable new revenue through payments in lieu of taxes (PILOTs), incentivize continued investment, and meet the County’s economic development goals.

Bottom line: Property owners could now face greater year-to-year fluctuations in tax rates as the equipment depreciates. The agreement was intended to provide more predictable County revenue while supporting continued investment in the region. We look forward to continued discussions with local jurisdictions on how to maximize the economic benefits of these investments while protecting sustainable, long-term tax revenues

recentPosts.text:
We're sharing new data on how AI is changing research at OpenAI.

We find researchers' AI use continues to rise exponentially, and agents are completing longer tasks, but human involvement remains central in research. Researchers are also spending more time on safety and alignment, with human effort in these areas growing faster than in any other individual research area.

This report aims to increase transparency around research acceleration and inform the governance of increasingly capable AI. We believe that AI labs should be required to track and publicly report indicators of recursive self-improvement (RSI): the process by which AI accelerates the development of future AI systems. 

Our hope is that this expanded report will help sustain and advance shared measurement norms across the industry.

https://t.co/xyGPcCkPCK
We’re sharing how we approach safety at every stage of a model’s lifecycle, from early research to internal use to public deployment.

Working with @AMD, our models identified up to 14% PPA improvement on flagship GPU IP in less than five months—building on designs AMD’s engineers had already spent years optimizing.

The same approach helped improve Jalapeño, our first custom inference chip, with gains verified on real silicon.

bio: We're on a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Support: @MicrosoftHelps

recentPosts.text:
I can finally share what I’ve been working on at @Microsoft. I lead Today, the product you saw all over the Ignite conference this week.

Today is a new form factor for work. It’s not a chat box it’s a Feed. While you sleep, an AI agent works in the background on your email, your calendar, Teams and your documents. In the morning, the work is already prepared: replies drafted, conflicts spotted, the messages that matter pulled to the top, the documents waiting for your review.

You don’t have to prompt it. There’s nothing to configure. You open Today, check what it did, and in a few taps you send, accept or mark as done. Most of us start the day by digging through everything that came in overnight. With Today, you start by finishing work your agent did.

We think this is what AI at work should feel like: proactive, quiet and useful, without you having to ask.

Today lives in your existing apps starting with Outlook and Copilot meeting customers in the app they use the most.

I had so much fun building it with an incredible team: @JesseProvo, @donovanso, @telmen, @justinchando, Chris Parnin, Gideon Ojo, Alex Trzyna, Christopher Miller, Diana Slaba, Kirill Varshavskiy. Thank you for the craft, the late nights, and for caring about every detail.

And none of this would have happened without the incredible support of @sumit_c, @elbio_abib, @rroslansky, @clamanna, @jacobandreou and so many others across Microsoft. Thank you for believing in it.

This is just the beginning!

P.S. i made a little film to celebrate. It starts in 1997. Watch till the end.

I enjoyed meeting Cardinal Fabio Baggio for an episode of #ToolsAndWeapons to discuss Pope Leo XIV's encyclical letter, Magnifica Humanitas (Magnificent Humanity), and a fundamental question it raises: How do we ensure AI serves humanity, rather than people becoming servants to the technology we've created?

It's a theme that I've been hearing from people everywhere I travel. They have real concerns about where AI is taking us and how we can ensure human intelligence remains central to shaping its future. @Microsoft
